children: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas isn't likely to raise its policy rate by 50 bps later this month, despite the unexpectedly high September CPI print, Barclays economist Brian Tan says in a note. Headline CPI rose 7.2% from a year earlier in September, up from August's 6.1% increase. The central bank's stance remains hawkish, he notes. Still, Tan reckons that concerns over sluggish domestic economic growth outlook will discourage policymakers from pushing for a larger rate increase to quell inflation pressures. 2Q GDP growth slowed to 2.3% from 1Q's 2.8% expansion. Barclays continues to expects BSP to deliver a 25bp rate hike in October and now forecasts another 25bp increase in December. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
